extracted.intended_audience: agency rule-makers, public commenters, regulatory attorneys, and others interested in federal rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on participating in and evaluating federal agency informal rulemaking (notice-and-comment) including procedural requirements, doctrines that govern permissible changes between proposal and final rule, and practical tactics for preserving issues for judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Procedure Act §553 framework
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage-by-stage view of informal (rather than formal) proceedings; encompasses the notice-and-comment process that governs most federal rulemaking. Relevant to what procedural steps agencies must take and what commenters must do to participate effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical outgrowth doctrine
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'logical outgrowth' doctrine and what makes a final rule a permissible variant of the proposed rule
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines limits on how much an agency may change a proposal before the final rule departs from what was noticed; key for evaluating whether an agency provided adequate notice and whether the final rule can be sustained on review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise general statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'concise general statement' requirement and how agency response to comments shapes review
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must provide a concise statement of the rule's basis and purpose; the adequacy of the agency's responses to comments is central to judicial review of whether the statement and rulemaking were adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-rulemaking proceedings (ANPRMs, RFIs)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance notices and requests for information are formalized opportunities to shape the record early; participation at these stages can affect both substance and preservation of issues for later review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negotiated rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Negotiated rulemaking under the Negotiated Rulemaking Act
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A collaborative process statutory framework for developing rules by negotiation among stakeholders and agency representatives; changes the dynamics of participation and the administrative record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct final rulemaking and interim final rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct final rulemaking and interim final rules
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different procedural paths for issuing rules (e.g., direct final rules intended to be noncontroversial; interim final rules sometimes adopted without prior notice-and-comment); each path imposes different opportunities and risks for commenters and reviewability issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB/OIRA review role
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive Office review that can affect timing, substance, and interagency coordination in rulemaking; relevant for understanding external influences on agency decisionmaking and procedural posture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions for rulemaking (5 U.S.C. § 553(e))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statutory mechanism for members of the public to request that an agency commence rulemaking; important as an alternative path to influence agency action and to create a record of concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard look review (State Farm)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hard look review (State Farm) and what it means for the comment record
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts require agencies to take a 'hard look' at relevant evidence and reasoned explanation of choices; the administrative record and comment responses are crucial to demonstrating that hard look review has been satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte communications and disclosure rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex parte communications and disclosure rules
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules governing off-the-record communications with decisionmakers and requirements for disclosure to the docket or parties; these constraints affect fairness of the process and what information is part of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of confidential information in dockets
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of confidential information in dockets
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How agencies handle privileged or confidential submissions in the public docket, including redaction, protective treatments, and interplay with FOIA and court review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserving issues in the docket for judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: The importance of preserving issues in the docket for judicial review
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters must raise issues timely and clearly in the record to preserve them for later litigation; strategic framing and timing of submissions affects reviewability and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to respond doctrine
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'duty to respond' doctrine - agencies must respond to significant comments
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies are required to respond to significant or material comments in their final rule; failure to address significant comments can render a rule vulnerable to judicial reversal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic timing of submissions across rule stages
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic timing of submissions across rule stages
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides commenters on when to submit material (e.g., pre-proposal, proposal, post-proposal) to maximize influence and preserve legal arguments; timing can affect whether comments are considered 'significant' and part of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket records as the basis for litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: How docket records become the basis for litigation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The administrative docket constitutes the record upon which courts review agency action; completeness and quality of the docket determine the strength of judicial review and litigation strategy.
